# The Thief of Stars

## Scripture
"This is what the Lord says—he who appoints the sun to shine by day, who decrees the moon and stars to shine by night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar—the Lord Almighty is his name." — Jeremiah 31:35

## Reflection
Some nights, we forget the stars are still there. Clouds roll in, and the sky becomes a gray lid. The familiar constellations—Orion, the Big Dipper, Cassiopeia—are hidden from view. Yet not one star has vanished. They remain fixed in their courses, blazing faithfully beyond the veil.

Clouds are thieves in a way. They steal our view of what was always there. As August's lingering haze settles over the summer sky, we might feel similarly obscured in our spiritual lives. Circumstances gather like cumulus layers, blocking our sense of God's presence. We wonder: *Has He stopped shining on me?*

But God's covenant with creation—that sun, moon, and stars will keep their appointed rhythms (Jeremiah 31:35-36)—mirrors His covenant with you. Your circumstances may shift like weather systems, but His faithfulness is as permanent as the stars themselves. The "thief of stars" doesn't steal the stars—only the seeing of them.

When the clouds part tonight—and they will—the same stars you saw last summer will be there. Likewise, when your season of obscurity lifts, you'll find God exactly where He's always been: fixed, faithful, and shining just for you.

## Prayer
Lord, when clouds obscure my view, help me remember that You remain. I trust that Your faithfulness outlasts every storm, and I wait with hope for the clearing sky. Amen.
